articles.title: Technology Platform Genius AI Expands by 14K SF at 838 Broadway
articles.narrative: Genius AI, a technology platform, has expanded its headquarters at 838 Broadway in New York City by 13,754 square feet, bringing its total footprint to 27,373 square feet across the entire second and third floors. This expansion also brings the six-story building to full occupancy. The tenant's broker noted the company's strong momentum and recent fundraising success as drivers for the increased physical space.

data_points.notable_features: Located between East 12th and East 13th streets, just south of Union Square.
data_points.project_notes: Genius AI previously occupied 13,619 square feet on the second floor since 2024. The building underwent recent renovations and repositioning.

articles.title: Rick Gropper of Camber Property Group: 5 Questions
articles.narrative: Camber Property Group, an affordable housing developer, is celebrating its tenth year in business with two significant projects in New York City. The firm has commenced construction on the $167 million redevelopment of Chelsea Beacon, transforming the former Bayview Correctional Facility into 131 affordable and supportive housing units with community spaces. Additionally, Camber was selected for the $62 million modernization of NYCHA's Unity Towers in Coney Island. These projects highlight the firm's expertise in redeveloping distressed assets and creating new affordable housing, contributing to the city's ambitious housing goals.

data_points.address: 550 West 20th Street, New York City, NY
data_points.notable_features: Redevelopment of a historic building, formerly a YMCA and then a women's correctional facility, into affordable and supportive housing with community facilities.
data_points.project_notes: The building was abandoned after Hurricane Sandy in 2012. The project involves adding approximately 10 floors on top of the existing structure.

articles.title: Rise of the Data Center ‘Wildcatters’
articles.narrative: A new trend of "wildcatters" is emerging in the data center industry, where entrepreneurs acquire and prepare land for future data center development by securing power access, zoning approvals, and utility connections. These individuals and firms then sell these "powered land" sites to hyperscalers and developers, capitalizing on the immense demand for data center infrastructure. This strategy, likened to oil wildcatting, involves significant capital investment and coordination with utility companies to transform raw land into development-ready sites, often in more rural areas with cheaper land and fewer regulations.

articles.title: Sunday Summary: Are GLP-1s Affecting Retail? Oh, You Better Believe They Are.
articles.narrative: This article explores the transformative impact of GLP-1 weight-loss drugs on the retail sector, noting a significant shift in consumer spending habits. Data indicates an 8-10% reduction in spending at fast-food outlets, coffee shops, and on sweets, leading to closures and bankruptcies among traditional restaurant chains. Conversely, there's a notable increase in traffic to organic markets and gyms, with fitness center membership attrition rates flattening. This trend is directly influencing real estate deals, with wellness and fitness concepts actively seeking space. The article also highlights the success of luxury retailers engaging Gen Z through social media and collaborations, as well as the thriving experiential retail sector, which focuses on providing immersive entertainment and memory-making experiences rather than traditional anchor tenancy models. Additionally, several trophy office properties in Midtown Manhattan have recently hit the market, signaling a potential shift in investment opportunities, while major real estate firms like SL Green Realty and Blackstone reported strong earnings, driven by high occupancy rates and strategic investments in AI-related sectors.

articles.title: Outdated office buildings in Minneapolis-St. Paul? They’re finding new life as apartments, industrial facilities
articles.narrative: A new report from Newmark highlights a significant trend in the Minneapolis-St. Paul market: the conversion and demolition of outdated office buildings. Since 2020, 73 office properties totaling 7.6 million square feet have been removed from the market, with another 570,000 square feet proposed for removal through 2028. This shift, driven by post-pandemic changes in workplace demand, has seen residential development as the leading conversion type, followed by industrial facilities. Government incentives and the suitability of older buildings in downtown areas for residential reuse are fueling this adaptive transformation.
articles.market_intelligence: The Minneapolis-St. Paul office market has seen 7.6 million square feet removed since 2020, representing nearly 5.8% of the region's office inventory. Residential conversions account for 2.7 million SF of former office space, while industrial conversions total 2.1 million SF. Class B office buildings are the primary targets, with 6 million SF removed, making up 9% of that segment. Corporate campuses have also contributed significantly, with 2.2 million SF removed or converted since 2020.

articles.title: Texas Icon Raymond J. Kane: Structuring real estate to endure beyond the closing
articles.narrative: This article profiles Raymond J. Kane, a founding director at Kane Russell Coleman Logan PC, highlighting his four-decade career in commercial real estate law. Kane is recognized for his expertise in structuring projects, relationships, and institutions to ensure their long-term endurance through market cycles and generational changes. His practice focuses on real estate, lending, corporate, and federal taxation matters, with a particular emphasis on leasing and construction across various commercial development phases. Kane's approach is rooted in principles learned from navigating past economic disruptions, emphasizing adherence to legal frameworks, fulfilling commitments, and nurturing professional relationships.

articles.title: Berkadia brokers sale of 450-bed student housing property in Huntsville
articles.narrative: Berkadia has brokered the sale of The Forum at Sam Houston, a 450-bed student housing property in Huntsville, Texas. The garden-style asset was sold by Preiss to CrestMarc, a Texas-based firm. Berkadia also arranged the financing for the acquisition.

data_points.address: 3019 S Sam Houston Ave, Huntsville, TX

articles.title: JLL Capital Markets closes sale of Medicine Lake Apartments in Plymouth
articles.narrative: JLL Capital Markets has successfully brokered the sale of Medicine Lake Apartments, an 81-unit lakefront multifamily community in Plymouth, Minnesota. The property, known for its unique direct access to Medicine Lake and private boat slips, was sold by Bigos Management to Weber Organization. This transaction highlights the appeal of well-maintained assets in highly desirable suburban markets with strong local amenities and proximity to major employers.

data_points.address: 1300 W Medicine Lake Dr., Plymouth, MN
data_points.notable_features: Lakefront community with 12 private boat slips, 24-hour fitness center, sauna, outdoor pool, multi-sport court, resident clubroom, and direct access to the Luce Line Regional Trail. Located near three Fortune 500 headquarters and within the top-ranked Wayzata School District.

articles.title: UBS and CBRE sign leases at Opus’ Arcadia office building in Edina
articles.narrative: Opus' Arcadia office building in Edina, Minnesota, currently under construction, has reached 71% preleased status with significant commitments from UBS Financial Services Inc. and CBRE. UBS will occupy the entire fifth floor, while CBRE has leased a portion of the third floor. Opus and its affiliated companies will also take a substantial amount of space, including the entire top floor. The strong leasing momentum reflects continued demand for high-quality office environments that offer exceptional amenities, premier locations, and a superior workplace experience.

data_points.notable_features: Class-A office building with a glass-façade, dramatic lobby, collaborative gathering spaces, conference rooms, employee training room, private tenant clubroom, fitness center, and a landscaped outdoor terrace with fire pits and grilling stations.
data_points.project_notes: Broke ground in September 2025 on the former Eden 100 site in Edina's Grandview District.
